widgetMetadata.instructions: Each entry under `widgets` describes one chart/widget rendered on this page of the Israeli Ecosystem dashboard. Descriptions are result-agnostic: they explain what the visualization shows and how to interpret it, not the specific numbers. The `dataPaths` array on each entry lists dot-notation paths inside this same JSON file where the underlying data for that widget lives (e.g. "kpis.patentingStartups" or "ipIntensity.items") When summarizing or answering questions about a number from this snapshot, locate the relevant widget(s) by `dataPaths` and quote the corresponding `description` to explain the metric. Widgets that have a 10 year trend usually show the total overall (across all years) and you get the exact data for each year in the past 10 years. The 10 year data do not add up to the total of course

unicorns:timeline.title: Israeli Unicorns by Year
unicorns:timeline.description: Every Israeli unicorn, meaning a company that crossed a $1B valuation, shown as its logo in a column for the year it crossed. The population is companies headquartered in Israel plus Israeli-founded companies whose headquarters later moved abroad, so a foreign company with only an Israeli R&D branch is not counted.

unicorns:industries.title: Unicorns by Industry
unicorns:industries.description: Israeli unicorns grouped by industry, drawn as a circle-pack bubble chart: each bubble is a subindustry sized by how many unicorns belong to it and colored by its parent industry. The industry legend above the chart is the color key. Hovering a bubble highlights the matching logos on the timeline above and dims the rest.

unicorns:velocity.title: Valuation per year to Unicorn
unicorns:velocity.description: The twelve companies that built the most value per year on the way to $1B, ranked by valuation at the crossing divided by years from founding. Bars are colored by industry, and each row shows the valuation and the years it took. Hovering a logo opens the same company card as the timeline. The metric deliberately measures value built per year rather than return on capital raised.

unicorns:status.title: Current Status
unicorns:status.description: Where every Israeli unicorn stands today: Active (still private), Acquired, IPO (publicly listed), or Closed (reached $1B, was never acquired or listed, then wound down). Being acquired or listed outranks later inactivity, so an acquired company whose standalone entity was later dissolved still counts as acquired. Colors match the status tags shown in the timeline popup.

unicorns:cohort.title: Where They're Based
unicorns:cohort.description: Israeli unicorns split by where they are headquartered: HQ in Israel versus Israeli-founded companies whose headquarters moved abroad. Foreign companies with only an Israeli R&D branch are not part of the unicorn population at all.

unicorns:time-to-exit.title: Founding to Exit
unicorns:time-to-exit.description: Every Israeli unicorn that was later acquired or went public, as a connected-dots row on a shared age axis in years: founding sits at zero, the first dot marks the $1B crossing, and the second marks the acquisition (green) or the IPO (yellow). The gap between the dots is the time from unicorn to that outcome. Rows are sorted by how quickly the company got there, with the median marked. The axis caps at 20 years so the fast movers stay readable. Companies whose recorded acquisition or listing predates their crossing are left out as bad source dates.

unicorns:time-to-unicorn.title: Years to Unicorn
unicorns:time-to-unicorn.description: Distribution of how many years companies took from founding to crossing the $1B valuation, in two-year bins with a final 16+ bucket, and the median marked. This measures time to unicorn, not time to exit: the snapshot carries no exit date.
